messages:
katie.su: FYI — getting a P1 from AcmePay. Their hosted inference requests are getting 503/500s across multiple regions starting ~08:12 UTC. They provided a few request IDs. Errors in gateway are upstream worker crashes/restarts.

katie.su: Example request IDs: r-8a3f2, r-8a3f7. Customer says this started after they bumped batch_size to 16 and increased prompt length. They attached a stacktrace and one dump.

leo (oncall): I'm on it. Which pool/cluster? Any recent deploys? @raman can you shadow?

katie.su: Affected pool: hosted-gpu-eu-west-2 (pools/gpu-large). No user-facing deploys from our side at 08:00, only infra autoscale events. Deploy bot shows a canary push at 06:45 unrelated.

raman (sre): grabbing logs. Initial glance: repeated SIGSEGV in upstream-runner, often followed by a container restart and immediate 503s at the gateway. Also some OOM messages from CUDA. Might be a memory leak for certain model variants when large batch + long context.

raman (sre): Logs snippet from runner stdout:
```
[2026-02-11T08:12:14Z] ERROR upstream-runner: Unexpected crash: signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
Backtrace (most recent call first):
  0x7f9c1f2a3b4c in infer::kv_cache::write()...
  0x7f9c2a1b9d00 in attention_kernel::compute()...
  CuDNN: returning CUDNN_STATUS_SUCCESS
  NVML: OutOfMemory on device 0 while allocating 234.5 MiB
```

mira (eng-runtime): can you paste the `dmesg` and nvidia-smi output around a crash? Need to see if kernel OOM or driver killed the process vs user-land segfault.

katie.su: attached customer dump and one nvidia-smi snapshot they captured. nvidia-smi shows memory spike to 99% then crash.

leo (oncall): Running quick repro against staging with batch_size=16, prompt length ~12k tokens. I can reproduce an OOM on a GPU with 48GB. Repro script: POST /v1/generate with array of 16 inputs each large context.

leo (oncall): Commands I ran:
```bash
kubectl -n hosted logs deploy/upstream-runner-abc --since=10m --previous
kubectl -n hosted exec -it pod/upstream-runner-abc -- bash -c "dmesg | tail -n 50"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
```

raman (sre): Repro logs show incremental memory growth across iterations (not instant allocation) -> likely leak or growth in KV cache + attention state when batch concatenation happens. Suggest throttle batch or enforce prefix cache eviction.

mira (eng-runtime): Possible causes: 1) regression in attention kernel for newer model quantization path, 2) our KV prefetch incorrectly retaining tensors across requests, 3) a CUDA driver subtle bug triggered by long sequence.

mira (eng-runtime): Short mitigation for hosted: add a runtime flag to cap per-worker token-memory with aggressive KV eviction and set default max_batch_size=8 in the affected pool. Also enable fallback policy to route requests > X tokens to a larger-worker-type or to a CPU-based queue.

ops-bot: Canary roll started for config change 'cap-kv-evict=true,max-batch=8' in pool hosted-gpu-eu-west-2 by mira at 08:35 UTC.

katie.su: Noted. I've told AcmePay to revert client-side batch_size to 4 and to reduce max_context for now. They can expect fewer 503s while we patch. Customer asked for ETA.

raman (sre): Rolling config change to the pool now. Monitoring nvml memory and restart rate. If restarts drop to <3/hr we'll call it mitigated.

leo (oncall): Quick hotfix test passed on one node — memory growth stabilized after forcing KV eviction every request. Canary at 10% of pool.

mira (eng-runtime): I'm opening a bug for 'kv retention w/ long sequences' and will assign a debug owner. Repro instructions for eng: minimal replay script that sends 100 loops of batch=12 12k tokens, with `--enable-prefetch` flag to reproduce leak locally.

mira (eng-runtime): Also, we'll add an automated guard: reject requests that would allocate > 70% of GPU memory based on predicted token matrix size with a 413-like response (client too large) instead of letting worker accept then die.

katie.su: Customer updated — they reverted settings and errors dropped. They've asked for root cause postmortem and SLA credit. I told them we'll follow up after eng confirms root cause.

raman (sre): Action items:
- mira: root cause triage & patch (ENG-4567) — owner mira, ETA 72h
- raman: complete host-level crash collection and attach core dumps to ticket — ETA 24h
- leo: extend monitoring alerts for worker restart rate threshold to 5/min in hosted pools — ETA 24h
- katie.su: coordinate customer comms and coordinate SLA request — ETA 48h

leo (oncall): If anyone needs more logs for specific request IDs, paste them here. I'll keep the mesos/k8s crash timeline until 09:30 UTC.

katie.su: Thanks all :thumbsup: Will update customer and escalate billing request once eng confirms.

ops-bot: Incident record created: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-0845 | Severity: P1 | Owner: mira (eng-runtime).
